P01.title: Patch Ivanti Connect Secure on vpn-gw-01 to close the VPN-to-domain-controller path
P01.summary: Validated path P01 starts at the internet-facing corporate VPN, vpn-gw-01 (Ivanti Connect Secure). Chaining CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 gave the validation agent an authenticated shell on the appliance. Admin credentials cached on vpn-gw-01 also worked on the IT jump host jump-it-01. The jump host admin group has RDP rights on the domain controller dc-01, and the agent opened a read-only RDP session there. Fixing vpn-gw-01 breaks the path at its first step.
P01.why_it_matters: Anyone on the internet could take over the corporate VPN, reuse its stored admin credentials on the IT jump host, and log on to the domain controller. Control of the domain controller would let an attacker create or change any account in the company, deploy ransomware broadly, and disrupt the IT systems the utility relies on to run. These flaws are widely exploited, including in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict access to the web and admin interfaces of the Ivanti Connect Secure appliance vpn-gw-01 so they are not reachable from the internet beyond what users strictly need, and apply the vendor's interim mitigation for these flaws.

Install the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887) on vpn-gw-01, following the KEV requirement to "apply mitigations per vendor instructions or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable."
Check vpn-gw-01 for signs of compromise using the vendor's integrity checker, and rebuild the appliance from a clean image if anything unexpected is found.

Remove the cached admin credentials from vpn-gw-01 and, with the Windows Server team, reset that account's password on jump-it-01 and anywhere else it is used, then revoke active VPN sessions so users re-authenticate.
verify_steps: Confirm vpn-gw-01 reports the vendor's fixed release and the integrity checker shows no mismatched or new files.
Confirm the old admin credentials taken from vpn-gw-01 are rejected on jump-it-01.
Ask the validation team to rerun path P01 and confirm it no longer reaches the VPN appliance shell or the domain controller.
P01.exec_line: An internet attacker could break into our corporate VPN and reach the server that controls all company accounts; patching the VPN closes this.
P01.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel.

P02.title: Patch the field office Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN (vpn-gw-02) to break the confirmed path to the domain controller
P02.summary: Validated path P02 runs from the internet to the domain controller dc-01. An out-of-bounds write in the Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02 (CVE-2024-21762) gave an unauthenticated foothold. The Windows Print Spooler flaw on file and print server fs-02 (CVE-2021-34527) then gave SYSTEM rights. On fs-02, a cached domain admin logon was present, and that credential reaches dc-01. Fixing the entry point on vpn-gw-02 breaks the whole path.
P02.why_it_matters: An outside attacker with no password could go from the field office VPN to full domain admin control of Active Directory, which governs logons to nearly every corporate system. That would let them disable or encrypt systems across the utility, disrupt business operations, and stage further attacks toward operational networks. Both flaws are widely exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, limit exposure of the Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02: restrict access to the SSL-VPN interface to known field office source addresses, or disable the SSL-VPN web interface until it is patched.

Upgrade FortiOS on vpn-gw-02 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2024-21762). If no fix can be applied, follow the KEV requirement to "discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable" and move field office users to another remote access path.
After upgrading, check vpn-gw-02 for signs of compromise: unexpected admin accounts, configuration changes, unknown files or processes, and unusual outbound connections since February 2024.
Terminate all active VPN sessions and reset the local admin credentials and any VPN user credentials stored on vpn-gw-02.
verify_steps: Confirm vpn-gw-02 reports the vendor's fixed FortiOS release and that the SSL-VPN interface is reachable only from the approved source addresses.
Run an authenticated vulnerability scan against vpn-gw-02 and confirm CVE-2024-21762 is no longer reported.
Ask the validation team to rerun path P02 and confirm it no longer reaches fs-02 or dc-01.
P02.exec_line: A flaw in our field office VPN could let outsiders take over our core login system; Network Engineering is patching it now.
P02.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel asset.

P03.title: Patch and reset sessions on Contractor gateway (nsg-01) to close path to email server
P03.summary: Validated path P03: an attacker on the internet can exploit CVE-2023-4966 on the Contractor gateway (nsg-01, Citrix NetScaler Gateway). The gateway leaks session tokens, which let a contractor session be taken over. From that session the attacker reached the Email server (exch-01, Microsoft Exchange Server), which answered the server-side request forgery check for CVE-2022-41040. Fixing nsg-01, the entry point, breaks the whole path.
P03.why_it_matters: An outsider who hijacks a contractor session gets inside the corporate network and can reach the company email server. Control of email would expose internal communications and credentials and give a foothold for ransomware across the utility's business systems. Both flaws are widely exploited and tied to known ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict access to the Contractor gateway (nsg-01, Citrix NetScaler Gateway) to known contractor source addresses, or take its Gateway virtual server offline until it is patched.
Upgrade nsg-01 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2023-4966).
Right after the upgrade, kill all active and persistent sessions on nsg-01, as the CISA KEV required action demands, so stolen session tokens stop working.

Check nsg-01 for signs of compromise: review session logs for sessions reused from unexpected addresses, and ask the Messaging team to review exch-01 access logs for activity from contractor sessions.
Reset passwords for all contractor accounts that had sessions on nsg-01 while it was vulnerable.
verify_steps: Confirm in the nsg-01 management console that the installed build is the fixed release and that no sessions older than the session kill remain.
Confirm that the access restriction on nsg-01 stays in place until the fixed build is verified.
Ask the validation team to rerun the validation of attack path P03 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P03.exec_line: A flaw in the contractor remote access gateway lets outsiders hijack sessions and reach our email server; Network Engineering will patch and reset sessions.
P03.route_reason: The path ends at exch-01, the Email server, which is not marked crown_jewel, so the ticket goes straight to the owning team.

P04.title: Patch internet-facing plant edge firewall fw-edge-03 (PAN-OS GlobalProtect, CVE-2024-3400) to cut path to the data historian
P04.summary: Validated path P04 starts at fw-edge-03, the plant edge firewall running Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS with GlobalProtect exposed to the internet. Command injection on the GlobalProtect portal (CVE-2024-3400) was confirmed. The firewall's management account password is the same as the local admin password on ot-jump-01, the IT to OT jump host, and the plant data historian hist-01 accepts logons from that jump host. The validation agent stopped at the OT boundary and did not log on to ot-jump-01 or hist-01.
P04.why_it_matters: An outside attacker could take full control of the plant edge firewall, then use the reused password to get onto the OT jump host and from there into the plant data historian. That would put operational data, and a foothold inside the OT environment, in the hands of an attacker, with real risk to plant visibility and operations. This flaw is widely exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, on fw-edge-03 (Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS), enable the vendor's Threat Prevention signatures for CVE-2024-3400 on the GlobalProtect interface, and restrict access to the GlobalProtect portal to known source addresses where possible.
Upgrade PAN-OS on fw-edge-03 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2024-3400).

After patching, check fw-edge-03 for signs of compromise, including unexpected files, configuration changes, new accounts and unusual outbound connections, and escalate to incident response if anything is found.
Change the fw-edge-03 management account password to a unique value, and notify OT Engineering so they rotate the matching local admin password on ot-jump-01 to a different unique value.
verify_steps: Confirm fw-edge-03 reports the vendor's fixed PAN-OS release and that the Threat Prevention signatures for CVE-2024-3400 remain active on the GlobalProtect interface.
Confirm with OT Engineering that the fw-edge-03 management password and the ot-jump-01 local admin password no longer match.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P04 to confirm it is closed.
P04.exec_line: An internet-facing plant firewall can be taken over and used to reach our plant data historian; patching it and changing a reused password closes this.
P04.route_reason: The path ends at hist-01, the plant data historian, which is marked as a crown jewel, and passes through ot-jump-01, also a crown jewel.

P05.title: Patch SQL injection in Progress MOVEit Transfer on vendor file exchange (mft-01)
P05.summary: The validation tool confirmed an internet-reachable SQL injection (CVE-2023-34362) in the Progress MOVEit Transfer web app on mft-01, the vendor file exchange. The test read only the version table, but the flaw gives an unauthenticated attacker access to the MOVEit database. The path is a single step, so fixing mft-01 closes it.
P05.why_it_matters: Anyone on the internet could read, change or delete the MOVEit database on the vendor file exchange, exposing the files, accounts and records the utility shares with its vendors. That could leak sensitive operational or customer data and give a foothold for ransomware, which has been widely used against this exact flaw.
fix_steps: Today, restrict inbound web access to Progress MOVEit Transfer on mft-01 so only known vendor and internal addresses can reach it, or take it off the internet until patched.
Apply the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2023-34362) to Progress MOVEit Transfer on mft-01.
After patching, check mft-01 for signs of compromise: unfamiliar files in the web application folders, unknown or recently created MOVEit user accounts, and unusual file downloads in the MOVEit logs.
Reset credentials for MOVEit administrator and service accounts on mft-01, and rotate the database account the application uses.
verify_steps: Confirm in the Progress MOVEit Transfer admin console on mft-01 that the installed release is the vendor's fixed release for CVE-2023-34362.
Confirm from an outside address not on the allow list that the mft-01 web interface is not reachable, if access was restricted.
Ask the validation team to rerun path P05 against mft-01 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P05.exec_line: Our internet-facing vendor file exchange has a widely exploited flaw exposing shared data; we are restricting access and patching it now.
P05.route_reason: The path ends at mft-01, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes directly to Enterprise Applications.

P06.title: Close internet-exposed admin setup on Partner wiki (wiki-ext, Confluence Data Center, CVE-2023-22515)
P06.summary: Validation confirmed that the setup endpoint on the Partner wiki (wiki-ext, Atlassian Confluence Data Center) is reachable from the internet and would allow anyone to create a Confluence administrator account through CVE-2023-22515. The agent stopped before creating an account. Fixing wiki-ext closes this path.
P06.why_it_matters: An outsider could make themselves an administrator of the Partner wiki and read, change or delete everything shared with partners, including any project documents, contacts or credentials stored there. Admin control of an internet-facing server also gives an attacker a foothold to plant malicious content for partners or staff and to probe further into the utility. This flaw is widely exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, restrict internet access to the Partner wiki (wiki-ext) so the Confluence setup and administration pages cannot be reached from outside, or take the site offline until it is patched.
Upgrade Atlassian Confluence Data Center on wiki-ext to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs; if that is not possible, discontinue use of the instance, as CISA requires.

Check wiki-ext for evidence of compromise, as the KEV entry requires: review the administrator group for unknown or recently created accounts, and review recently installed plugins and recent configuration changes.
Remove any unauthorized accounts, reset passwords for legitimate administrators, and report any positive findings to CISA and the security team.
verify_steps: From an external network, confirm the Confluence setup endpoint on wiki-ext is not reachable or returns access denied.
Confirm the Confluence version shown in the wiki-ext administration console matches the vendor's fixed release, and that the administrator list contains only approved accounts.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P06 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P06.exec_line: Our partner wiki can be taken over by anyone on the internet; we are restricting access and patching it now.
P06.route_reason: The path ends at wiki-ext, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes straight to the Collaboration Tools team.

P07.title: Close internet-exposed ScreenConnect setup wizard on rmm-01 (path to ESXi cluster esxi-07)
P07.summary: Validation confirmed that the ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote support console (rmm-01), which faces the internet, exposed its setup wizard without authentication (CVE-2024-1709), allowing creation of an administrator account. From that foothold, an attacker could create the directory group that the VMware ESXi virtualization cluster (esxi-07) trusts for administration (CVE-2024-37085) and take full control of the hypervisors. Fixing rmm-01, the entry point, breaks the whole path.
P07.why_it_matters: An outsider could take over the remote support console and use it to gain full control of the virtualization cluster that runs many corporate servers. That would let them shut down, encrypt or steal from those systems at once, disrupting business operations across the utility. Both weaknesses are used in real ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict access to the ConnectWise ScreenConnect console on rmm-01 so it is not reachable from the internet, allowing only the service desk's approved addresses or VPN.

Apply mitigations per vendor instructions by upgrading ScreenConnect on rmm-01 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2024-1709), or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.

Check rmm-01 for compromise: review all ScreenConnect user accounts and remove any administrator accounts that were not created by the IT Service Desk, and review session and audit logs for unexpected activity.
Reset passwords for all ScreenConnect accounts on rmm-01 and any directory credentials stored on or used by the console, and end all active sessions.
verify_steps: From an external network, confirm the ScreenConnect console and its setup wizard on rmm-01 are no longer reachable without authentication.
Confirm the ScreenConnect version on rmm-01 matches the vendor's fixed release and that the account list contains only approved administrators.
Request a rerun of the validation of path P07 to confirm it no longer succeeds.
P07.exec_line: An internet-facing remote support tool could let outsiders take over our server virtualization cluster; we are locking it down and patching it now.
P07.route_reason: The path ends at esxi-07, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so the ticket goes directly to the IT Service Desk as owner of rmm-01.

P08.title: Remove internet exposure and patch Cisco IOS XE web UI on substation router rtr-sub-12 (path P08)
P08.summary: Validated path P08 starts at the Substation comms router (rtr-sub-12), whose Cisco IOS XE web UI is reachable from the internet and runs a version affected by CVE-2023-20198. From that router, a route leads to the Energy management system data link (ems-link-01) with no access list between the substation comms network and the EMS data link. Fixing the router breaks the path at its entry point. No traffic was sent to the EMS link during validation.
P08.why_it_matters: An outside attacker could take full control of the substation router and use it to reach the energy management system data link, which carries grid operations data. That could let them interfere with how operators see or control the grid. This flaw is one of the most widely exploited router weaknesses.
fix_steps: Today, disable the Cisco IOS XE web UI on rtr-sub-12 or block it from the internet and all untrusted networks, so the router complies with BOD 23-02.
Upgrade Cisco IOS XE on rtr-sub-12 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2023-20198).

Check rtr-sub-12 to determine if it may have been compromised, including any unknown privilege level 15 local accounts or unexpected configuration changes, and immediately report positive findings to CISA.
Remove any unauthorized accounts and reset all local and administrative credentials on rtr-sub-12.
verify_steps: From an outside internet connection, confirm the rtr-sub-12 web UI no longer responds.
Confirm rtr-sub-12 runs the vendor's fixed release and that only approved local accounts exist.
Ask the validation team to rerun path P08 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P08.exec_line: An internet-exposed substation router could give attackers a route to our grid energy management system; we are locking it down and patching it now.
P08.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, the Energy management system data link, which is marked as a crown jewel.

P09.title: Patch Apache Log4j2 on the internet-facing Outage map API (outage-api) to close remote code execution path P09
P09.summary: Validation path P09 confirmed that the Outage map API (outage-api), an internet-facing Java service using Apache Log4j2, is exposed to CVE-2021-44228. A harmless lookup string sent in a request header caused outage-api to make an outbound DNS query, which shows the vulnerable Log4j2 lookup behavior is active and reachable from the internet.
P09.why_it_matters: Anyone on the internet could run their own code on the server behind the public outage map and use it as a foothold into the utility's network. That could let an attacker alter or take down outage information customers and crews rely on during storms, or steal data and move toward internal systems. This flaw is among the most widely exploited ever and has been used in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict outbound network traffic from the Outage map API (outage-api) so it can only reach the specific internal services and DNS resolvers it needs, blocking all other outbound internet connections until the patch is in place.

Upgrade Apache Log4j2 in the outage-api Java service, including any copies bundled inside application archives or dependencies, to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2021-44228), then redeploy. If it cannot be updated, remove outage-api from the network, as KEV allows only updating or removal, with temporary mitigations acceptable only until updates are available.

After patching, review outage-api application, web and outbound connection logs back to when the service was deployed for signs of compromise, such as unexpected lookup strings in requests, unusual outbound connections, new files or new processes.
Rotate any credentials, API keys and certificates stored on or used by outage-api, and escalate to incident response if any sign of compromise is found.
verify_steps: Confirm through a software inventory or dependency scan that every Log4j2 component in the deployed outage-api build, including bundled copies, is the vendor's fixed release.
Confirm the outbound traffic restriction for outage-api is in place and that blocked outbound connections are being logged.
Ask the validation team to rerun attack path P09 against outage-api and confirm it no longer triggers an outbound lookup.
P09.exec_line: Our public outage map server has a well-known flaw that lets outsiders take control; we are patching it and checking for intrusion.
P09.route_reason: The path ends at outage-api, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes directly to the Customer Applications team.

P10.title: Restrict and patch Fortinet FortiManager fmgr-01 exposed to the corporate user network (CVE-2024-47575)
P10.summary: Validation path P10 confirmed that the device registration port on the Firewall manager (fmgr-01, Fortinet FortiManager) answers from the corporate user network and runs a version affected by CVE-2024-47575, a missing authentication flaw. An unauthenticated attacker on the corporate network could run code on fmgr-01 and take over the firewall manager. This is a single-step path, so fixing fmgr-01 closes it.
P10.why_it_matters: The firewall manager holds the configuration and credentials for the firewalls it manages and can push policy changes to all of them. An attacker who controls it could quietly open firewall rules, steal device credentials, and use that access to move toward sensitive operational networks. This flaw is widely exploited.
fix_steps: Today, restrict the device registration (FGFM) port on Fortinet FortiManager fmgr-01 so it only accepts connections from the managed firewalls' addresses, and block it from the corporate user network.
Upgrade fmgr-01 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs, and enable Fortinet's mitigation that rejects registration attempts from unknown devices.
After the upgrade, check fmgr-01 for signs of compromise: unknown registered devices, unexpected admin accounts, and configuration or policy changes that no one on Network Engineering made.
Rotate the admin passwords on fmgr-01 and the credentials of every firewall it manages, since those stored credentials may have been exposed.
verify_steps: From a host on the corporate user network, confirm the fmgr-01 device registration port no longer answers.
Confirm fmgr-01 reports the vendor's fixed release and that the unknown-device registration block is enabled.
Request a rerun of validation for attack path P10 to confirm it is closed.
P10.exec_line: Our firewall management system can be taken over from the office network; Network Engineering will restrict access and patch it now.
P10.route_reason: The path ends at fmgr-01, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes directly to the owner team, Network Engineering.

P11.title: Patch Netlogon (Zerologon) on domain controller dc-01
P11.summary: Validation confirmed that domain controller dc-01 (Microsoft Windows Server, Active Directory) runs a version affected by CVE-2020-1472 and accepts Netlogon secure channel connections from corporate workstations. The agent checked the version only and made no change. The path is a single step, so patching dc-01 closes it.
P11.why_it_matters: Anyone on the corporate network could take full control of the domain controller and, through it, every account and Windows system joined to the domain. That would let an attacker deploy ransomware across corporate IT and reach any business or operations systems that rely on Active Directory logins. This flaw is widely exploited and has known ransomware use.
fix_steps: Today, turn on Netlogon secure channel enforcement mode on dc-01 so it refuses vulnerable Netlogon connections, and note any legacy devices that are denied.
Install the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2020-1472) on dc-01, then on every other domain controller in the domain, per Microsoft's instructions.

After patching, check dc-01 for signs of compromise: unexpected domain controller machine account password changes, new or changed privileged accounts, and Netlogon events showing vulnerable connections from workstations.
If any sign of compromise is found, reset the dc-01 machine account password and the krbtgt account password twice, and escalate to incident response.
verify_steps: Confirm the Windows update addressing CVE-2020-1472 shows as installed on dc-01 and all other domain controllers.
Confirm enforcement mode is active on dc-01 and the Netlogon event log shows vulnerable connection attempts being denied.
Ask the security team to rerun validation of path P11 against dc-01 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P11.exec_line: Our main corporate login server has a well-known flaw that lets anyone inside the network take over all accounts; the Identity team must patch it now.
P11.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, which is marked as a crown jewel asset, so the ticket needs human review before assignment.

P12.title: Restrict RDP and require MFA on OT jump host ot-jump-01 to close corporate path to the EMS data link (P12)
P12.summary: The validation tool confirmed that the RDP logon prompt on ot-jump-01 (IT to OT jump host, Microsoft Windows Server, OT DMZ) is reachable from a corporate desktop VLAN and accepts password-only sign-in with no multi-factor prompt. ems-link-01 (Energy management system data link) trusts logons that come from ot-jump-01, so anyone who signs in to the jump host can move on to the EMS data link. The tool did not attempt a logon, and no credential was found or reused. No CVEs are involved; this path rests entirely on configuration.
P12.why_it_matters: Anyone on the corporate network who obtains a single password could sign in to the OT jump host and, through its trusted connection, reach the energy management system data link. That link carries grid operations data, so tampering with it or disrupting it could affect visibility and control of the grid and trigger reliability and regulatory consequences for the utility.
fix_steps: Today, restrict inbound RDP to ot-jump-01 at the IT to OT firewall so that only a small, named set of approved administrator workstations or a dedicated admin subnet can connect, and block it from all corporate desktop VLANs.
Enforce multi-factor authentication for every RDP sign-in to ot-jump-01, and limit the accounts allowed to log on remotely to a named OT Engineering group.

Review logon records on ot-jump-01 for RDP sessions from corporate desktop addresses and for any unexpected onward connections to ems-link-01, and escalate anything unexplained as a possible compromise.
If unexplained sessions are found, end any active sessions and reset the passwords of the accounts involved.
verify_steps: From a host on a corporate desktop VLAN, confirm that the RDP port on ot-jump-01 can no longer be reached.
From an approved administrator workstation, confirm that signing in to ot-jump-01 requires a second factor and that an account outside the allowed group is refused.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P12 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P12.exec_line: Any corporate computer can reach the gateway to our grid energy management system with only a password; we are locking it down.
P12.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, the Energy management system data link, which is marked as a crown jewel. The fix point ot-jump-01 is also a crown jewel.
